meeting_header: Date/Time: 2026-07-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Michael O'Neal (Cedar Brook Head of IT), Sara Kim (Cedar Brook CCO), Daniel Ruiz (Cedar Brook Cloud Architect)
summary: Initial discovery on Cedar Brook Bank's data residency and compliance requirements. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII/financial data. Main concerns: where logs and prompts are stored, auditability, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/SAML, and network isolation. Agreed to send security docs and schedule technical deep dive for private deployment and PoC scope.
topics: Logging and audit log retention & redact options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
POC scope and benchmarks (latency, throughput, model variants)
Regulatory controls: GLBA, SOC2, PCI considerations
transcript: 00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. Quick intros, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and Priya is our solutions engineer. 00:08 Michael: Hi, Michael O'Neal, Head of IT at Cedar Brook. We've got Sara, our compliance lead, and Daniel, cloud architect on the call. 00:15 Sara: Hi. 00:17 Priya: Hey all, big thanks. We wanted to focus today on data residency, logging, and any compliance blockers. 00:25 Daniel: Yep, we have a fairly strict posture, bank, midwest operations, most of our customer data must remain in US regions, some state-level rules too. 00:34 Alex: Understood. High level, are you evaluating Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Or all three? 00:41 Michael: All three — we're trying to map risk profiles. Hosted is easiest but we worry about logs and model prompt retention. Dedicated might be middle ground. Private is preferred for prod but heavier ops. 00:51 Sara: From compliance, our big questions: where logs live, can you prevent customer prompts being used for model training, do you provide audit logs for access and admin actions, and KMS integrations. 01:03 Priya: Good callouts. We have offerings: hosted with contractual data controls (no training on customer data), dedicated pools with tenant isolation, and private which gives you data plane control in your VPC or on-prem. 01:12 Michael: Do you support HSM-based keys? We need hardware-backed keys for custody. 01:17 Alex: Yes, we integrate with common KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, customer HSM via KMIP). For private installs you can bring-your-own HSM and Redwood's control plane is optional. 01:28 Sara: How about audit logs — admin actions, who accessed models, tokenization events — can those be exported to our SIEM? 01:36 Priya: Audit logs are available; we stream to customer endpoints or S3, with retention configurable. We also emit admin/event traces for rollouts and model changes. For hosted customers we keep operational logs for X days by default but can extend under contract. 01:51 Daniel: X days? Can we set that to 7 years if compliance asks? 01:55 Priya: Long-term retention is possible in Dedicated/Private; hosted can have contract provisions but long retention with hosted is less common due to cost. We'll capture requirements. 02:06 Michael: Another big one — prompt/data residency. Do prompts or generated outputs ever leave the customer's region for processing? 02:12 Alex: Processing can be region pinned. Hosted API default region is tied to the customer account; we have multi-region routing but you can require US-only. For Private, everything stays in your network. 02:23 Sara: And what about logs that Redwood keeps for troubleshooting? Are there PII redaction capabilities? 02:29 Priya: We support automatic redaction patterns and manual redaction tooling. For Sensitive PII we offer automated detectors that can redact before logs leave your VPC, plus a managed redaction service during PoC if needed. 02:40 Michael: Any chance that prompts are used to improve public models? We can't have customer financial PII used in training. 02:45 Alex: We contractually prohibit using customer prompts for training. We also offer contractual clauses and can provide a data handling attestation. 02:52 Sara: We will want that in writing and evidence — like a data flow diagram showing where tokens land and how we can request deletion. 02:59 Alex: We'll send SOC2 + ISO docs and a network/dataflow diagram. 03:05 Daniel: On the networking side, for Private, how does routing work? Can we do VPN peering or private link? 03:11 Priya: We support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and site-to-site VPN. For on-prem we can do air-gapped installs; that takes more planning. 03:20 Michael: Performance wise — if we go private, do we lose latency, or does Redwood provide optimized runtime? 03:26 Priya: The runtime is GPU-optimized; private installations can run the same optimized engine. Latency depends on your infra but we work with customers to tune batching, KV cache, and kernel selection. 03:35 Alex: Also worth noting the tradeoff: hosted gives fastest go-live, dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives reserved throughput, private gives maximum control but more ops. 03:46 Sara: For auditability, we need immutable logs and chain-of-custody. Can the logs be write-once and exported to our SIEM without Redwood being able to edit? 03:56 Priya: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3 with ACLs and lifecycle rules. For strong non-repudiation you'd keep the log store within your account; for hosted customers we can push logs to your customer-managed storage to meet that requirement. 04:12 Daniel: Tokenization and KV cache — are cached prefixes persisted to disk? Does that contain PII? 04:18 Priya: KV cache holds context to speed generation; we recommend redacting sensitive fields before caching. For private/dedicated we can disable persistent KV cache or encrypt it with your keys. 04:29 Michael: Ok. Also interested in role-based access controls and SSO. We use Okta. 04:34 Alex: We support SAML/Okta, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with audit trails. 04:40 Sara: HIPAA — we have a small team that handles health-adjacent data for some clients. Is Redwood HIPAA friendly? 04:46 Priya: We support HIPAA with BAAs for Private and Dedicated customers; hosted can be covered under specific agreements. We'll follow up with specifics. 04:54 Michael: Any compliance with GLBA / PCI? 04:57 Alex: GLBA controls are commonly requested for banks; we can map Redwood features to control families. PCI is more about card data handling — we'd recommend tokenization and strict redaction before sending to models. 05:09 Sara: Can you do targeted redaction rules for account numbers or routing numbers? 05:13 Priya: Yes, customizable regex detectors, plus ML-based entity detectors tuned for financial entities. 05:20 Daniel: On tenancy isolation — if we go dedicated, how isolated is it? Shared management plane but isolated inference pool? 05:27 Priya: Exactly. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation for inference, while the control plane is multi-tenant but logs/metrics and data paths are segregated. 05:36 Michael: If we want absolute separation, private is the way. For cost reasons we might try dedicated first. 05:42 Alex: Makes sense — many customers pilot on dedicated then move critical workloads to private. 05:47 Sara: For our auditors, we will want sample attestations and the ability to run a small audit or get a SOC2 Type II report. 05:55 Alex: We'll share SOC2 Type II and related attestations. 05:58 Daniel: For the PoC, can we do a small throughput benchmark with PII redaction in place and measure latency at our edge? 06:05 Priya: Yes, we can run a PoC: ingest a redacted prompt set, enable redaction, run latency and throughput, and capture logs to your SIEM. We'll need network access details. 06:16 Michael: Timeline — we are hoping for a pilot in August, production by end of Q4 if it all lines up. 06:22 Alex: That's reasonable. We'll send materials this week and set up the SE deep dive. 06:26 Sara: One more thing — data residency at the state-level: some records must stay in-state. Can Redwood support that granularity? 06:33 Priya: For hosted, region-level (state-level) is harder; dedicated/private can be deployed into specific cloud regions or on-prem to meet state residency. We can document options. 06:45 Michael: Ok that's helpful. 06:47 Alex: To recap next steps — Alex will send SOC2, ISO, network diagram, and pricing; Priya will schedule deep technical session and prep VPC/on-prem notes; Daniel and Sara will send compliance questionnaire and region requirements. 06:59 Sara: Thanks everyone. 07:01 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
